title: What falls outside the answer?
lines: A hospital can shorten its queue while the patient's most important concern remains unasked.
Cones of Meaning uses a simple image: every idea opens a view while leaving something outside it.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Keep a visible semantic boundary and something relevant outside it; avoid presenting the cone as literal brain anatomy.
voiceDirections: Speak with quiet concern; lightly emphasize most important concern remains unasked. Present this specific idea in a simple conversational voice, without a grand announcement or dramatic suspense, and leave a natural pause.
Speak with plain interest; lightly emphasize opens a view. Present this specific idea in a simple conversational voice, without a grand announcement or dramatic suspense, and leave a natural pause.

visual.meaning: A hospital room, queue display, patient and clinician ground the opening. The queue arrow moves while the unasked concern remains beside the chair. A clear triangular view and boundary then introduce the cone as a metaphor for selective attention.

title: The frames we inherit
lines: AI gives this familiar problem new urgency by producing plausible explanations faster than people can examine them.
The book follows scientific ideas, shared stories, and the institutions that make those stories powerful.

Speak with engaged clarity; give gentle emphasis to stories powerful. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.

title: When ideas travel
lines: It asks what changes when a technical insight becomes a metaphor everyone starts repeating.
A comparison can help us see something new while making it sound more certain than it is.

title: Look around the clarity
lines: Confident explanations become more interesting when you can see how they direct your attention.
